description: Annotates every image in a directory with a zero-shot model — no training, no class supports. SAM3 (default) detects with free-text concepts, visual exemplar boxes, or both; INSID3 takes exemplars drawn on a few images as references and segments the same classes in every image. Optionally tiled (SAHI) for large imagery with small objects, via the zero-shot-annotation Tapis app.

inputs.name: annotation_file
inputs.description: Optional: an existing annotations/exemplar-prompt JSON to use for exemplar prompts — wiring this in populates the panel's 'Prompt file' field (the annotation_file config key, same name as this port) with its path instead of having to browse/type it by hand, and flips the panel to Exemplar-prompts mode so it's actually visible. Only useful for a directly-wired DESIGN-TIME node (its own system/path config, e.g. smart_labeler, source_json_file, or the annotation_format_adapter's 'converted' output) — see the panel; an upstream JOB step's output isn't resolvable at design time.

outputs.name: annotations
outputs.description: The run's annotations_<model>_<timestamp>.json — filenames carry a timestamp, so the actual file is resolved (via a real Tapis directory listing once the job finishes) from inside the 'annotations' output directory rather than being a static path; see file_glob. The glob's '[!c]' deliberately excludes annotations_coco_<model>_<timestamp>.json (written alongside it when output_format is 'coco'/'both') by assuming the model name doesn't start with 'c' — true for every backend registered today (sam3). If that ever changes, or you specifically need the coco file with output_format='both', browse the run's archive directory manually instead of this port.

prompt_mode.description: Which kind of prompt drives detection. 'text' uses free-text concepts typed below. 'exemplar' uses visual exemplar boxes (plus optional paired text) from an uploaded prompt file — SAM3 finds more objects like them in the SAME image. 'reference' (INSID3) reads the same prompt file's exemplars as references and segments those classes in EVERY image; the panel pairs it with model 'insid3'. UI-only — doesn't change what's sent to the job; text_prompts and annotation_file are independently included whenever set, so the two can be combined (insid3 ignores text prompts).

text_prompts.description: Free-text concepts to detect, applied to every image (e.g. tree, "parked car", "solar panel"). Each detection is labelled with the prompt that found it, or with the label you give it: dog -> german shepherd prompts the model with 'dog' and writes 'german shepherd' to the annotations (stored as "dog=german shepherd"). Several prompts can share one label. At least one of text_prompts or annotation_file is required.

annotation_file.description: Full tapis://system/path URI of a JSON file with per-image exemplar boxes (SAM3 geometry prompts; for insid3, the references — optionally with object polygons) and/or additional text prompts. A Smart Labeler or COCO annotation file also works as-is: every annotation becomes an exemplar for its label (polygons kept, Smart Labeler flag 'negative' = negative box), keyed by its image path. Exemplar boxes are absolute pixel coordinates in a specific image, keyed by path relative to the image directory, bare filename, or 'default'. At least one of text_prompts or annotation_file is required. Stored as a URI rather than a bare path + separate 'system' field precisely because this key doubles as an INPUT PORT NAME: when the port is wired, _resolve_inputs overwrites this config value with the upstream output's URI at run time, so the two forms have to be interchangeable. Auto-filled from the wired 'annotation_file' input when connected — see that input's description — but can still be browsed/typed by hand; an explicit edit here always takes precedence over the wired value.

model.description: Backend model from the zero-shot registry. 'sam3': text and exemplar prompts, per image. 'insid3': training-free in-context segmentation on a frozen DINOv3 (github.com/visinf/INSID3) — the prompt file's exemplars are references, and every image is segmented for each class.

model_id.description: Checkpoint override for the chosen backend. sam3: a HuggingFace checkpoint, blank uses facebook/sam3. insid3: the DINOv3 backbone — dinov3_vits16, dinov3_vitb16 or dinov3_vitl16 (blank = dinov3_vitl16) — which must match the insid3_weights checkpoint when one is given.

insid3_weights.description: insid3 only, optional. Blank downloads the backbone in model_id from the Hugging Face Hub (facebook/dinov3-<backbone>-pretrain-lvd1689m, gated — needs hf_token, see below). To use an original checkpoint instead, give the full tapis://system/path URI of the DINOv3 .pth for that backbone (dinov3_vitl16_pretrain_lvd1689m-8aa4cbdd.pth for the default, from github.com/facebookresearch/dinov3). Staged into each job (~1.2 GB for vitl16), so clear it when switching back to sam3.

insid3_image_size.description: insid3 only. Square resolution images (or tiles) are resized to. 1024 is INSID3's default; 768 is faster with a small accuracy drop.

reference_box_masks.description: insid3 only. INSID3 needs an object MASK per reference; polygons in the prompt file are used as-is. For a box with no polygon: 'sam3' segments the object inside the box with the SAM3 tracker (needs the HF token below), 'box' uses the filled box — quicker, but background inside the box leaks into what the model looks for.

min_area.description: insid3 only. INSID3 returns one mask per class, split into connected components — one annotation each (touching objects come out as one). Components smaller than this many pixels are dropped; 0 keeps all.

is_sahi.description: Slice each image into overlapping tiles before inference (SAHI) — improves detection of small objects in large imagery. Tile count grows quickly: images x prompts x tiles inferences per run.

tile_size.description: Tile size in pixels. Only used when SAHI is enabled.

overlap_ratio.description: Fractional overlap (0-1) between adjacent tiles, so an object spanning a tile boundary is still fully captured in at least one tile. Only used when SAHI is enabled.

exemplar_tile_mode.description: With SAHI + exemplar prompts: 'intersecting' runs only tiles holding a positive exemplar (skipped tiles are logged). 'all' runs every tile, falling back to the exemplar's paired text on tiles with no visible exemplar (recorded as prompt_type 'text'). Only used when an annotation_file is set.

exemplar_min_visibility.description: Minimum fraction (0-1) of an exemplar box's area that must fall inside a tile to count as visible there; the box is then clipped to the tile. Only used when an annotation_file is set.

batch_size.description: Tiles per inference batch (not images — batches fill across images). Higher values are faster but use more GPU memory; a CUDA OOM falls back automatically to one tile at a time for that batch.

confidence.description: Minimum score (0-1) for keeping a detected instance. Not used by insid3, which makes its own foreground decision (its scores still rank detections for NMS).

mask_threshold.description: Threshold (0-1) for binarising predicted masks before they're turned into polygons. Not used by insid3.

nms_iou.description: IoU threshold (0-1) for merging detections across tiles and prompts via Non-Maximum Suppression.

class_agnostic_nms.description: Let detections from different prompts suppress each other during NMS, collapsing a text prompt and an exemplar prompt that both find the same object into a single box. Off by default, so each prompt keeps its own annotation.

no_segmentation.description: Skip mask-to-polygon extraction — boxes only, faster.

output_format.description: 'flat' matches the rest of this repo's annotation format. 'coco' writes standard COCO images/annotations/categories JSON. 'both' writes each.

max_images.description: Annotate at most this many images — useful for smoke tests. 0 annotates every image.

hf_token.description: Team secret holding a HuggingFace access token with access to the gated facebook/sam3 checkpoint (huggingface.co/facebook/sam3 — request access, then create a token under HF account settings). Add it via the dashboard's secrets settings, then pick it here; passed to the job as the HF_TOKEN env var. Leave unset only if the checkpoint is already cached on the exec system and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is set. insid3 needs it too, unless insid3_weights is set and reference_box_masks is 'box': the token's account must also have accepted the DINOv3 license on the backbone's model page (e.g. huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m).

fileInputs.name: prompt_file
fileInputs.description: Optional: exemplar/text prompt JSON, staged in when annotation_file is set. Note this text is itself placeholder-substituted (job_spec renders every string leaf, descriptions included), so it deliberately spells no placeholder out literally. sourceUrl is the annotation_file value verbatim — always a full tapis://system/path URI, whether it came from this node's own config (the panel stores the system inside the URI, see zeroShotAnnotation.tsx) or from the wired 'annotation_file' input, which _resolve_inputs overrides the config value with at run time. Re-adding a 'tapis://' + system prefix here (as this did while the config key was still named prompt_file) doubles the scheme on the wired path.

fileInputs.name: dinov3_weights
fileInputs.description: insid3 only: the DINOv3 backbone checkpoint, staged in when insid3_weights is set. sourceUrl is the insid3_weights value verbatim — a full tapis URI, like annotation_file.
